brief:
Middle East Eye examined the experience of Gaza-based journalists who have won international recognition for their coverage of the conflict, even as they face severe humanitarian conditions including famine and displacement. The outlet posed the question of what it means to receive prestigious awards like Emmy nominations for reporting on genocide while enduring the same crisis firsthand.

The reporting highlights the stark contrast between global recognition of journalistic work documenting the conflict and the daily survival struggles of those producing that coverage from within Gaza.
dek: The Gaza Podcast: Winning an Emmy while starving What does it mean to win an award for your reporting on the genocide - while living in the midst of the genocide and famine?
title: Gaza journalists win Emmy amid famine, displacement
